Proprioceptive nerve endings detect joint position and movement. Articular cartilage is avascular and aneural, so it lacks proprioceptors. The synovial membrane primarily contains pain fibers, not proprioceptors. The joint capsule contains mechanoreceptors like Ruffini endings that respond to stretch, and ligaments contain Golgi tendon organ-like endings that detect tension. Articular discs have limited innervation and are not primary sites for proprioception. Thus, the main locations are the capsule and ligaments.

The diagnostic stage of the Box-Jenkins methodology evaluates model adequacy by examining residuals and using overfitting tests. Statement (i) is true because diagnostics can indicate underfitting (via residual autocorrelation) or overfitting (via parameter insignificance). Statement (ii) is true as residuals are checked for autocorrelation, heteroscedasticity, and non-normality. Statement (iii) is true because an adequate model yields residuals with no autocorrelation structure. Statement (iv) is true because overfitting tests should show insignificant coefficients if the model is appropriate.
